questions.q: What does this lesson add on top of what Flow Designer & Automation already covered about IntegrationHub?
options: Why it's a licensed add-on, and the two real value propositions behind what you were already using
A full re-introduction to what a Flow is, from scratch
A new way to build Flows that replaces everything from course 4
Nothing — it simply repeats the earlier lesson
questions.explain: Course 4 showed you how to use a generic REST step and a spoke action; this chapter explains what IntegrationHub actually is and why, and goes deeper into building custom actions.

questions.q: What does it mean that IntegrationHub is licensed "the same commercial pattern as Performance Analytics"?
options: It's a separately-licensed add-on, not automatically included in every ServiceNow edition
It is free in every edition with no restrictions
It can only be purchased alongside Performance Analytics
It has nothing to do with licensing at all
questions.explain: Like Performance Analytics in the Reporting & Dashboards course, IntegrationHub requires its own license entitlement before a customer can use it.

questions.q: What is value proposition one that IntegrationHub adds?
options: Spokes — pre-built, ServiceNow-maintained action packages for specific external systems
A faster version of the Table API
A replacement for Authentication Profiles
A built-in MID Server
questions.explain: Spokes package pre-built actions for systems like Slack or Workday, maintained by ServiceNow rather than hand-rolled by the customer.

questions.q: When would you reach for IntegrationHub's generic REST/SOAP step instead of a Spoke?
options: When no official spoke exists for the external system you need to call
Only when building a Scripted REST API
Never — the generic step is deprecated in favor of Spokes
Only inside the MID Server
questions.explain: The generic REST/SOAP step exists precisely for systems without an official spoke, letting you build a custom integration inside the flow canvas.

questions.q: Before Spokes existed, what did connecting a Flow to a system like Slack require?
options: Hand-rolling a REST Message, hand-coding the auth handshake, and maintaining it as the API changed
Nothing — Flow Designer handled it automatically with no configuration
Only a generic SOAP step, never REST
A dedicated MID Server install for every external system
questions.explain: Before a Spoke replaced it, the customer had to hand-build and maintain the integration using a REST Message and manual authentication handling.
